name: Specified Skilled Worker visa (特定技能, types i and ii)

requirement_groups.name: Type i (up to 5 years, no family)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires working in one of the officially designated labor-shortage industry sectors (a list that has expanded significantly in recent years, spanning care work, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, food service, and several others).

This requires passing a sector-specific skills test and a Japanese language test (JFT-Basic or JLPT N4 or higher), unless exempt via completion of the Technical Intern Training Program (or its successor) in a matching field.
requirements.fix_path: Take and pass the required skills and language tests.

requirement_groups.name: Type ii (renewable, family allowed, path to PR)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires working in one of the (narrower) set of sectors eligible for Type ii status, which has also expanded in recent years beyond the original construction and shipbuilding fields.
This requires an advanced skills test demonstrating supervisory-level proficiency, typically after time spent on Type i status in the same field.
requirements.fix_path: Gain experience on Type i status and pass the Type ii advanced skills test.

evidence_required.document: Japanese language test result (JFT-Basic or JLPT N4+)

outcome.duration_length: Type i: up to 5 years total, not renewable beyond that cap; Type ii: renewable indefinitely

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan — 特定技能制度 (Specified Skilled Worker system)

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL SPLIT worth flagging prominently: Type i and Type ii are functionally almost two different routes bundled under one visa name — Type i is capped at 5 years total, permits NO family accompaniment, and does NOT lead to PR/citizenship (route-level outcome reflects this terminal Type i default); Type ii removes all three of those restrictions via the group-level outcome_override. This is one of the sharpest within-route outcome divergences in the entire dataset, comparable in scale to Portugal's Golden Visa investment-category variation but here driven by a skill-tier upgrade rather than investment amount. The designated labor-shortage sector list has genuinely expanded significantly in recent years — the exact current 2026 sector count/list was not fully itemized at tier-1 precision during this research pass (a real sourcing gap, flagged rather than guessed); re-verify against the current isa.go.jp sector list before treating this as exhaustive. This route is the primary downstream destination for jp_ikusei_shuro graduates once that program is fully operational from April 2027 — see that route's notes for the transition mechanics.
